chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hafiz al-Ju'abi told us, saying: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Muharibi told us, saying: 'Ubad ibn Ya'qoub told us, saying: Ali ibn Hashim told us, from his father, saying: The saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his Family, "Whoever I am his Mawla, then Ali is his Mawla," was mentioned in the presence of Zaid ibn Ali [ibn al-Husayn], peace be upon them both,
he said: He appointed him as a banner, so that the Party of Allah, Exalted and Glorious, might be known by it during the schism.
ai.seo_question: How did Zaid ibn Ali interpret the Hadith of Ghadir regarding the identity of the Party of God?
ai.summary: Zaid ibn Ali (peace be upon him) interprets the Hadith al-Mawla not merely as a title of affection, but as a divinely appointed standard (‘alam) to distinguish the true Party of Allah (Hizbullah) during times of sectarian division. This interpretation underscores the Shia view of Imamate as a necessary criterion for identifying the authentic community amidst the fragmentation of the Ummah. The narration highlights the continuity of prophetic authority through Ali, framing his leadership as the definitive marker of divine guidance.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	We were told by Muhammed bin Umar, the Keeper, al-Ju’abi, that he said: We were told by Abu Abdillah, Muhammed bin Qasim al-Muharibi, that he said: We were told by ‘Ubad bin Ya’qoub, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hashim, from his father, that he said: At the presence from Zaid bin Ali bin Hussain, peace be upon them both, it was mentioned the saying of the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family: Whoever I am his Leader, then Ali is his Leader.
He said: He assigned him as banner, that the Party of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, might be known with it during the schism.
